description: The plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers of a neural network model, comparing four distinct components: `attn_output`, `attn_residual`, `ffn_output`, and `ffn_residual`. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the model’s layers. The y-axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” ranges from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200, indicating the magnitude of the highest activation observed per layer. The `ffn_residual` (solid red line) shows a sharp rise starting at layer 5, peaking near 1600 around layer 15, and then dropping sharply after layer 20. The `attn_residual` (dotted orange line) follows a similar trajectory but with slightly lower peaks and a more gradual decline. The `ffn_output` (dashed green line) exhibits intermittent spikes—most notably around layers 6, 14, and 22—but remains near zero for most layers. The `attn_output` (dash-dot blue line) remains close to zero across all layers, with only a minor rise near the final layers. The plot highlights the dominance of residual connections (particularly FFN) in driving high activation magnitudes, while attention outputs remain relatively inactive throughout the model depth.
